caseName: The 100 kN booster taken through its start and shutdown transients, against the published RS-25 sequence
linkedCaseNote: The chamber pressure, throat area, flow rates and chamber volume are the propulsion hub's design point as built out by combustionDevices. Restated here so the example runs standalone; a cross-domain test asserts the residence time still matches what combustionDevices computes.

engine.startsRequiredNote: A first stage booster lights once. The restart case is run as a comparison because it changes the igniter answer completely.

feed._comment: Liquid volume downstream of the main propellant valves, which has to be primed at start and arrives in the chamber at shutdown whatever the controller does. Representative for a booster with the valves close-coupled to the injector; it is an assumption and it is registered as such.
feed.volumeNote: 8 litres between the main valves and the injector face

conditioning._comment: The wetted metal mass on the oxidiser side: the line, the valve, the pump and the injector manifold. LOX is the only cryogen in this engine; RP-1 is stored at ambient and needs no conditioning, which is half of why kerosene boosters are operationally simpler.

sequence._comment: A candidate start sequence for this engine, in seconds from the start command. Checked for ordering and for spacing against the RS-25 tolerance.

shutdown._comment: Oxidiser leads the fuel closed, so the transient runs fuel-rich. The lead is compared against the RS-25's one second hold.

ignitionDelays._comment: The delay cases compared, in seconds. 'hypergolic slug' is what a TEA-TEB cartridge achieves; the spark cases bracket what a torch igniter does on a cold engine.
